verdict.rationale: E2B's docs explicitly document pausing a sandbox and resuming it later 'from the exact state it was in, including the filesystem and the memory, so running processes and loaded variables survive,' with paused sandboxes kept indefinitely, plus CLI support for snapshot/pause management (e2b sandbox snapshot, list --state paused). This directly matches the story's core claim. missing for 10: independent/hands-on third-party verification of state fidelity after resume, and more detail on any limitations (e.g., GPU/network state, long-running process edge cases) beyond first-party docs.
